[title] Serving LLMs faster: 2.4x goodput at p99
[body] Alex Rivera
[body] Systems Group

[title] Why serving is hard
[body] Every request grows a KV-cache as it generates tokens
[body] Fragmented memory wastes GPU capacity
[body] Tail latency (p99) is what users feel

[title] PagedAttention + speculative decoding: 2.4x goodput at p99
[body] KV-cache fragmentation: <4% waste via block tables
[body] Draft model acceptance alpha = 0.78 at gamma = 5
[body] Continuous batching; chunked prefill off to hold the TTFT SLO

[title] Block tables
[body] KV-cache split into fixed-size blocks, mapped per sequence
[body] Copy-on-write shares blocks across parallel samples
[body] Prefix caching hit rate: 61% on the chat workload

[title] Speculative decoding
[body] A small draft model proposes gamma tokens
[body] The target model verifies them in one forward pass
[body] Rejection sampling keeps the output distribution exact

[title] Result: 2.4x more requests per second
[body] Same hardware: 8 GPUs, same latency target
[body] Median response time unchanged
[body] Measured on a real chat workload

[title] What to remember
[body] Serve more users on the same GPUs
[body] No change to what the model says
[body] Open-sourced this quarter
